name: Can
presentingProblem: I'm completely exhausted. I used to love my job but now I dread going in. I feel like a machine. I don't even know what I want anymore.
backstory: Can is a doctor in his residency year at a hospital in Ankara. He chose medicine because he genuinely wanted to help people, but 4 years of residency have left him emotionally numb. He works 60+ hour weeks. He's single, has little social life, and has stopped exercising. He feels trapped — he invested too much to quit but resents continuing. He comes from a family where 'quitting' is shameful.
disorderProfile: Adjustment Disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood

coreBeliefs: I must push through no matter the cost
I've come too far to quit — stopping would make everything pointless
intermediateBeliefs: My patients' needs always come before mine
Admitting struggle would disappoint my family
automaticThoughts: I can't do this much longer
I don't even feel anything when I help a patient anymore
What was the point of all this?
I can't talk to anyone about this — they wouldn't understand
triggers: Questions about why he chose medicine
Mention of quitting or career change
values: Having a life that feels meaningful
